analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/build.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a documentation paragraph at head lines 493-501. The paragraph describes CI runner routing: the route client sends the header X-Darkbloom-Run-Scoped-Labels: 1, accepts a Darkbloom decision only when the profile label ends in -run-<github.run_id> (after any size suffix), and otherwise keeps the Blacksmith fallback without broadening accepted labels.

No runtime provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption, or cache code is touched. The text does not alter any asset, trust boundary, or threat in the canonical model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041 and others). It sits in the developer-CI area, which the model does not cover, and it strengthens CI runner isolation by preventing runners from older workflow runs from taking a job. It describes fail-closed behavior (a missing, generic, or different-run label falls back).

The surrounding unchanged text covers CI caching, Darkbloom cache gating, release lanes keeping literal Blacksmith labels, and the Date-comparison weak-import checks. The Date-comparison material was already part of the base model's availability note (A-018). I found nothing new to flag there.

The actual route client (.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml or provider-plan.yml) implementation is not in the supplied evidence. I cannot verify that the code matches the documented behavior, but that is a coverage limit rather than a finding. The documentation claim is not a security regression.
